arguments.assumptions: Hypothetical FY2026 US-GAAP diluted EPS stress grid, not consensus or management guidance. Reported H1 2026 GAAP diluted EPS is $1.75. Bear/base/bull EPS of $3.40/$3.65/$3.90 therefore require H2 residual EPS of $1.65/$1.90/$2.15 on a constant-share approximation. Management's dated Q3 guidance is non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.06-$1.08 and cannot be added directly to GAAP H1 because exclusions are not forecast-reconciled. Bear tests slower AI/cloud deployments, customer timing, gross-margin pressure and a Q3 miss versus non-GAAP guidance; base assumes Q3 roughly consistent with management's non-GAAP range, continued AI networking and enterprise/campus growth, with a normal GAAP/non-GAAP gap; bull assumes AI fabric deployment pull-through, enterprise strength and operating leverage yielding a beat. P/E assumptions of 40x/50x/60x are explicit stress inputs chosen to test joint earnings and multiple compression/expansion around a high-growth networking cycle; they are not observed, historical-normal, fair or probability-weighted multiples. FY2026 ends after the 63-session mandate, so the grid is a forward run-rate sensitivity rather than a prediction that all earnings will be reported within the horizon.

cases.rationale: Miss stress: H2 GAAP residual $1.65; slower hyperscale/AI timing, customer concentration and margin normalization combine with multiple compression.
Operating continuation stress: H2 GAAP residual $1.90, with Q3 non-GAAP outcome broadly around company guidance and continued enterprise/campus plus AI demand; 50x is only a sensitivity anchor.
Beat stress: H2 GAAP residual $2.15 supported by stronger AI fabric deployments, enterprise/campus traction and operating leverage, combined with multiple expansion.
